game: The Flintstones: The Surprise at Dinosaur Peak!
note: No-Intro SHA1 of The Flintstones - The Surprise at Dinosaur Peak! (1994) (Taito).nes from the user's ROM library, the 16-byte iNES header and all, computed on this checkout with the README's command (python3 -c "from mep_build import _no_intro_sha1 as h; ...") over a 393232-byte file (NES header + 262144 bytes of PRG + 131072 bytes of CHR). The whole-file SHA1 of the same dump is FB9A9517AA8C76639B49FD1341488416F7265DEA - a different number for the same file, and the one the bootstrap builder stamps into <supportedRom> (ADR-0211). This dump is not the one the vendored cheat database names: UI/Dependencies/Internal/CheatDb.Nes.json's entry "Flintstones, The - The Surprise at Dinosaur Peak! (USA)" carries sha1 E5D64AEDDD25952804AF5447C6898E9191DB1614, and that field is a No-Intro hash - checked here by exact agreement for Castlevania (USA) (Rev A), Contra (USA), Life Force (USA) and Metroid (USA) against the same library - so the DB entry is a different dump of the same title and its 26 codes, among them the "Continue on Level 2..10" list, are not evidence about this ROM. The hash above is therefore the one computed on the file the sweeps actually ran on; no published pin is claimed for it. The selector this set is built on is the game's own hidden debug level select, typed as input (ADR-0239 s1 rung 1), so no RAM cheat rides with any route and there is no lives pin - ADR-0239 s3's inert control was not run because no pin was wanted. Mechanisms: only "a distinct area" is declared, and it is the one this set's own measurement shows - the debug screen's number loads a different room for each of its 37 values, and every session contributes drawn keys the others do not hold (ADR-0239 s5's union, runs/f1418/flintstones/RESULT.md). Nothing else on ADR-0182 s1's list is claimed: no boss and no cycle, because a 120 s blind body does not reach one and nothing in this set probed for it; no second player, because the sweep drives port 1 only, and the game's own second-controller lever - press Up on controller 2 during gameplay to end the level and mark it passed - was measured and did not fire; and no fusion or projectile-variant claim, because this set was not put through the F9.22 probe, and a mechanism nobody probed for is not evidence.
